title: Words that later changes on the branch made untrue: the Search Syntax table and footer, the Save Smart Folder line, and four sentences in the manual and README
problem:
Found by the review of the whole branch (20 Nov), in which one reviewer read all the improvements together through one lens and a second reviewer tried to refute each finding against the code. Nothing was run in that review: every finding was traced by reading. [every-word-must-match-strings-stale] Search Syntax dialog, manual table and README still say every word must match after lone letters stopped counting. The finder's scenario: Type `a budget` or `photo 2`. Since 5624239 the single letter or digit is not looked for: every budget, every photo is listed (the commit's own changelog and manual.md:370 say so). Press Cmd+/: the first row reads "Fuzzy words; every word must match (typos allowed)". docs/manual.md:358 says "Fuzzy words. Every word must match." twelve lines above the paragraph that says the opposite, and README.md:108 says "Fuzzy words, typo tolerant. Every word must match." Replacement: dialog "Fuzzy words; every word of two letters or more must match (typos allowed)" / "(typos off in Settings)"; manual.md:358 "Fuzzy words. Every word must match, but for a single letter or digit beside a longer word. Typos are allowed unless **Allow typos** is off."; README.md:108 "Fuzzy words; near misses with a typo when nothing else matches. Every word of two letters or more must match." The code path: src/finder/dialogs.rs:1028-1032 (the row's text) ; crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:2458-2465 (checked_words drops words shorter than two bytes when a longer one exists) used at :961 and :990-1002 (strict check and fallback) ; docs/manual.md:358 vs :370 ; README.md:108. Their evidence: src/finder/dialogs.rs:1028-1032: "Fuzzy words; every word must match (typos allowed)" / "(typos off in Settings)". crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:2457-2464: `let longer: Vec<String> = words.iter().filter(|w| w.len() >= 2).cloned().collect(); if longer.is_empty() { words.to_vec() } else { longer }`, used for the strict check and the fallback at :961 and :990-1001. The engine's own test pins the opposite of the row: engine.rs:4464 `assert_eq!(names("a budget"), budgets, ...)` where `Desktop/Budget.csv` has no `a` in its path, and :4469-4470 `photo 2` lists `photo 1.jpg`. docs/manual.md:358 "Fuzzy words. Every word must match." stands twelve lines above :370 "A single letter from A to Z, digit, or symbol beside a longer word isn't looked for". README.md:108 "Fuzzy words, typo tolerant. Every word must match." tests/controls.rs:1655 and :1663 pin the dialog's wording. Not recorded as known: typo-fallback-near-miss's reviewer wrote only that the row's "typos allowed" still holds, and final-pass-notes.md:65 is about the behaviour, not these strings. [save-dialog-kept-up-to-date-for-contents] Save Smart Folder says "Kept up to date." for a contents search, which is the one search that isn't. The finder's scenario: Search for a word, click Contents, press Cmd+S. The dialog reads "Shows files containing “word” on This Computer. Kept up to date." Save it and leave it showing: another program adds a file with the word; the list never changes until Cmd+R. The manual says so (manual.md:139 "A search by contents can take seconds, so it waits for Refresh", :665 "a search by name follows the files that come and go"), and commit 153eb8f's own message says it was written to make this line true ("The Save Smart Folder dialog says its results are kept up to date") but left contents searches out. The same line shows with Watch folders for changes off, when nothing follows. Should say it only for a name search, e.g. contents: "Shows files containing “word” on This Computer. Searched again each time you open it or refresh." The code path: src/finder/dialogs.rs:932-937 (format!("Shows {}. Kept up to date.", search.summary()) for every search) -> crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:425-456 (summary says "files containing" for contents) ; src/finder/mod.rs:1610-1617 (check_index_for_changes returns at once when self.search_contents) ; crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:659-662 (follow_changes: nothing reported with watch off). The second reviewer, who tried to refute it and confirmed it, corrects the scenario: The sentence is upstream's, not this branch's: 66c919b:src/finder/dialogs.rs:896 `format!("Shows {summary}, kept up to date.")`, shown for every search when no result followed anything. It meant that a Smart Folder searches again when opened, which still holds for a contents search: a click on its row ends the search and runs it again (filter.rs:330-342). 60df179 only reworded it. So the branch made it no worse; it made the line true while the search shows for name searches only. For a contents search, or with Watch folders for changes off, the list on screen stays as it is until Refresh or until the row is clicked again. Their evidence: src/finder/dialogs.rs:937 `.map(|search| format!("Shows {}. Kept up to date.", search.summary()))` for every search; crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:432-436 gives "files containing" for a contents search, so the line reads `Shows files containing “word” on This Computer. Kept up to date.` src/finder/mod.rs:1615 `if self.search_contents || self.searching || self.results_behind.catching_up { return; }` leaves a contents search out of what follows the index, and tests/finder.rs:1049-1063 (a_contents_search_is_left_to_refresh) pins that only Cmd+R brings the new file. With watching off nothing reports (engine.rs:660-662 `if !self.watch || !self.search_settings().watch { return true; }`). The only tests of the line are name searches (tests/controls.rs:3883, :4232). 153eb8f's message does give the line as a reason for the change. The smart-folder-save-and-leaks record describes the line, "files containing" included, without noting this. [search-syntax-footer-return] Search Syntax footer still says "Return searches now" though Return no longer runs a search whose results are in. The finder's scenario: Type words, wait for the results, press Cmd+/ and read the line under the table: "Searches run 50 ms after you stop typing; Return searches now and Down Arrow moves into the results." Since 17a460e Return with the results in searches nothing; it moves into the results as Down does, and only Refresh runs the search again (manual.md:333, :1003). Replacement: "Click an example to try it. Searches run 50 ms after you stop typing; Return and Down Arrow move into the results, waiting for them if they aren't in yet. Hidden files are only indexed inside git repositories." The code path: src/finder/dialogs.rs:1129 ; src/finder/mod.rs:1908-1930 (move_into_results: run_search only while search_waiting, otherwise enter_rows). The second reviewer, who tried to refute it and confirmed it, corrects the scenario: "Return searches now" is still true for a search waiting out its 50 ms pause (mod.rs:1919-1921), and Down Arrow now does that too. What is stale is the split between the two keys: both do the same thing, and with the results in neither runs a search. The manual (manual.md:333) says it rightly. Their evidence: src/finder/dialogs.rs:1129: "Click an example to try it. Searches run 50 ms after you stop typing; Return searches now and Down Arrow moves into the results. ...". src/finder/mod.rs:1896-1898 sends Return to `move_into_results`, and :1913-1929 reads `if self.results_pending() { ... if self.search_waiting { self.run_search(false, cx); } return true; } self.enter_results = None; if self.rows.is_empty() { return false; } self.enter_rows(window, cx);`, so with the results in Return searches nothing and moves in. Down Arrow calls the same function (src/finder/toolbar.rs:668). At the base Return always searched: 66c919b:src/finder/mod.rs:1308-1310 `// Return runs the search now and moves into the results. self.run_search(false, cx);`. The footer text is the base's (66c919b:src/finder/dialogs.rs:1003) with 06d84e9's first sentence added. No record mentions the footer; search-enter-before-results changed only the manual. [sorted-cut-ignores-folders-on-top] With Keep Folders on Top on, a sorted cut search leaves matching folders out and lists files that belong below them. The finder's scenario: Keep Folders on Top on (`folders_first` true). Use the fixture of tests/controls.rs a_sort_by_a_word_stays_with_the_names_that_have_it: folder `ledger`, files ledger.txt (5 bytes), my-ledger-notes.txt (3000), xledgerx.txt (200). Results shown 2; search `ledger`; click the Size header.
What happens: the list is my-ledger-notes.txt, xledgerx.txt with `2+ items`. The folder `ledger`, a match with the word in its name, is not listed. Name ascending behaves the same way: the first N names are chosen, and folders whose names sort after them are missing while files are shown.
What should happen: the window orders results folders first under every sort but Relevance. The manual says Keep Folders on Top "lists folders before files whatever the sort, in every view" (line 273) and that a sorted cut search "lists the first of every match in that order" (line 314). So `ledger` should be the first of the two rows, or the manual should say that the sort chooses before folders are put on top.
The mechanism is certain from the code; whether the engine or the manual is the thing to change is a judgment call, hence medium confidence. The code path: src/finder/mod.rs:1828-1834 sorts result rows by `listing::folders_on_top` and then `listing::compare`. src/finder/mod.rs:2203-2213 builds the `SearchRequest` with `sort` and nothing about folders first. crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:2166-2176 (`sort_before_cut`) orders the hits by `CutKey` and name only, and engine.rs:2077 (`cut_in_order`) cuts that list to the limit. crates/fffinder-core/src/listing.rs:158-164 is the rule the window applies afterwards to what is left. src/finder/list.rs:606-621 (`toggle_folders_first`, `folders_first_changed`) only re-sorts rows and never searches again. docs/manual.md:273 and :314 are the two promises. The second reviewer, who tried to refute it and confirmed it, corrects the scenario: The list is as the finder says, under Size descending and under Name ascending. The defect is narrower than the title: the engine choosing by the sort alone was decided in the brief, because with folders on top first, a broad search's matching folders would fill the list and no file would show. What is missing is one sentence in the manual's sort paragraph (docs/manual.md:314) saying that a sort chooses the items before folders are put on top. That is the finder's "smallest alternative"; the engine change it leads with is the one the plan rejected. Their evidence: Traced by reading; the list comes out as the finder says. But the behaviour is the plan's choice, not an oversight, so what is confirmed is a gap in the manual.

The path:
1. src/finder/mod.rs:2203-2213 builds the request with `sort: Some(self.result_sort)` and nothing about folders. `folders_first` occurs nowhere in crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs, and `SearchRequest` (engine.rs:199-223) has no such field.
2. engine.rs:2150-2154 keeps the names that have the word: `ledger`, ledger.txt, my-ledger-notes.txt, xledgerx.txt (4 > 2).
3. engine.rs:2172-2175 orders them by `a.cmp(b).then_with(|| listing::natural_cmp(a_name, b_name))`. The key is `CutKey::Size(hit.size, !hit.is_dir)` (2214) and a folder hit has size 0 (1937-1946), so by Size descending the folder is last. engine.rs:2077 cuts to 2.
4. The window then puts folders first only among the rows it was given: mod.rs:1828-1833 `listing::folders_on_top(&a.entry, &b.entry, folders_first).then_with(|| listing::compare(&a.entry, &b.entry, order))`.
5. src/finder/list.rs:618-621 `folders_first_changed` only rebuilds rows; it never searches.

Tests: tests/controls.rs:1095-1096 pins `["my-ledger-notes.txt", "xledgerx.txt"]` with folders_first at its default false (crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:297). No test has it on with a sorted search. The engine test at engine.rs:5500-5535 compares with `listing::compare` alone.

The plan decided this: /home/user/polish-tools/briefs/sorted-search-results.json, verifier, step 5: "Keep the client sort in `rebuild_rows` for Keep Folders on Top and the name tiebreak. Do not pass `folders_first` to the engine, or matching folders would crowd out files."

That decision is not carried into the done record, final-pass-notes.md or the manual. docs/manual.md:273 says folders are listed before files "whatever the sort", and :314 says a sorted cut search "lists the first of every match in that order", without saying which rule goes first. [f5-rows-and-mac-only-test] Manual's F5 rows don't match the Mac binding c27b4b5 added, and its test is a silent no-op off a Mac. The finder's scenario: On a Mac with split view on, put the keyboard in the search field (or the sidebar's tree) and press F5: the window refreshes, because c27b4b5 bound F5 to Refresh in the whole-window context there. docs/manual.md:916 says "Cmd+R | Refresh (F5 too, outside split view)" and :523 "Refresh (Cmd+R; F5 outside split view)"; the commit's changelog entry does not mention it either. Off a Mac the same rows overstate: F5 refreshes only with the keyboard in the file views. The one test, f5_refreshes_outside_the_file_views_on_a_mac, starts with `if !cfg!(target_os = "macos") { return; }`, so on Linux and Windows it passes having done nothing. Replacement for :916: "Cmd+R | Refresh. F5 refreshes too: in the file views outside split view, and on macOS anywhere else in the window"; for :523: "Refresh (Cmd+R; F5 in the file views outside split view)". The code path: src/actions.rs:139-151 (mac: key("f5", Refresh, &finder)) vs :180-181 (files: CopyToOtherPane; one pane: Refresh) ; docs/manual.md:523, :916, :952 ; tests/basics.rs:2690-2696. The second reviewer, who tried to refute it and confirmed it, corrects the scenario: Two of the finder's points are wrong. (1) The Mac's binding is tested everywhere, not only off a Mac: src/actions.rs:603-619 builds `key_table(true, cx)` on any system and asserts Refresh in the FINDER context is `["secondary-r", "f5", "secondary-r"]`; :621-635 is the off-Mac twin. CI also runs the UI test on macos-latest (.github/workflows/ci.yml:14). (2) The manual rows are upstream's, unchanged by the branch (66c919b:docs/manual.md:503, :882, :917; c27b4b5 edited one other paragraph). Off a Mac they overstated before the branch as they do now. On a Mac the commit message's reading is that F5 outside the file views already refreshed through View › Refresh in the menu bar, so the branch may have changed nothing there. Their evidence: src/actions.rs:144-151 binds `key("f5", Refresh, &finder, cx)` only `if mac`; :180-181 are the file views' F5 bindings. docs/manual.md:523 and :916 say "F5 outside split view" with :916 under "In the window". tests/basics.rs:2694-2696 `if !cfg!(target_os = "macos") { return; }`. Recorded as known and left in menu-bar-mac-keys, Found, not fixed: "The manual says F5 refreshes in the window (...) but on Linux and Windows F5 is bound in the file views only: with the keyboard in the search field, the sidebar or the tree it does nothing. A Mac refreshes there. ... this brief leaves Linux and Windows alone." Its behaviour_changes has the split view case ("it refreshes, in split view too, and copies nothing"), and its tests list has the UI test as "macOS only, returns early elsewhere: ... With the early return taken out it failed on Linux with Linux's table and passed with the Mac's".
proposal: Reproduce each fault first with a test that fails on the trunk. Then fix it. The finder's suggested fixes, as starting points and not checked plans: [every-word-must-match-strings-stale] Change the two strings in dialogs.rs, the two expectations in tests/controls.rs, manual.md:358 and README.md:108 as given. [save-dialog-kept-up-to-date-for-contents] In save_smart_folder_dialog append "Kept up to date." only when !search.contents (and search.watch is on); otherwise "Searched again when you open it or refresh." [search-syntax-footer-return] Replace the string as given. [sorted-cut-ignores-folders-on-top] Add `folders_first: bool` to `SearchRequest`, set it from `config.folders_first` in `start_search`, and have `sort_before_cut` put folders first when it is set; let `folders_first_changed` call `run_search` when the answer on screen says `sort_chooses`. Smallest alternative: one sentence in the manual's sort paragraph saying a sort chooses the items before folders are put on top. [f5-rows-and-mac-only-test] Reword the two manual rows as given; make the test body run everywhere by asserting the off-Mac half too (F5 in the search field refreshes nothing there) instead of returning.
original_test_plan: The finder's test ideas: [every-word-must-match-strings-stale] Unit test beside the dialog's rows (or in engine.rs): for the example the dialog's first row would be wrong for, search `a budget` in a fixture holding `Desktop/Budget.csv` and assert the row's meaning text does not claim every word matches when the hit has no `a`; simplest form: assert the dialog label contains "two letters or more". Fails today. [save-dialog-kept-up-to-date-for-contents] In tests/controls.rs: type `atlas`, click `by-contents`, click `save-smart-folder`, assert the `smart-summary` label does not contain "Kept up to date". Fails today. [search-syntax-footer-return] None worth keeping beyond a string check; behaviour is already pinned by tests/finder.rs:1503 a_second_return_before_the_results_are_in_opens_nothing. [sorted-cut-ignores-folders-on-top] Copy a_sort_by_a_word_stays_with_the_names_that_have_it with `folders_first` turned on before the search (through the config or the toggle_folders_first action), limit 2, query `ledger`, click `Size`, and assert `ui.names() == ["ledger", "my-ledger-notes.txt"]`. Today it is ["my-ledger-notes.txt", "xledgerx.txt"]. [f5-rows-and-mac-only-test] Off a Mac: Cmd+F, write a file into the folder, press F5, assert the file is NOT listed (the documented "key of the file views alone"); on a Mac in split view: same steps, assert it IS listed, against manual.md:916's "outside split view". Why the existing tests miss it: [every-word-must-match-strings-stale] tests/controls.rs:1655 and :1663 (search_syntax_says_whether_typos_are_allowed, from 06d84e9) pin the old wording, so the later engine change could not touch it without failing a test it had no reason to edit; README and manual tables are not tested. [save-dialog-kept-up-to-date-for-contents] tests/controls.rs:3883 and :4232 pin the line for name searches only; no test opens the dialog for a Contents search, and tests/finder.rs:1049 a_contents_search_is_left_to_refresh pins the opposite behaviour without looking at the dialog. [search-syntax-footer-return] No test reads the footer; 06d84e9 edited this very string (added "Click an example to try it.") after 17a460e and kept the rest. [sorted-cut-ignores-folders-on-top] Every sort test runs with `folders_first` at its default, false (crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:297). The engine test hits_are_sorted_before_the_cut_as_their_entries_are_listed compares the cut with `listing::compare` alone, without `folders_on_top`. [f5-rows-and-mac-only-test] The Mac behaviour is compiled out of the test everywhere this branch was run; src/actions.rs:622-635 pins only the order of the bindings off a Mac.
original_risks: This is a fix late in the branch: keep it to the fault. Every test on the trunk has to keep passing, and the improvements involved (live-search-results, menu-bar-mac-keys, search-enter-before-results, search-syntax-click-example, smart-folder-save-and-leaks, sorted-search-results, typo-fallback-near-miss) have tests that pin the behaviour around the fault: read their done records in /home/user/polish-tools/done/ before changing the functions they changed.

verifier.claim_check: A second reviewer traced the same path and confirmed it; neither ran anything. Reproduce before changing anything; if a test shows the fault is not there, write the closed record with the evidence and return skipped.

orchestrator_notes: This fault is in a change that is itself unreleased, so it gets no entry in CHANGELOG.md. In the commit message write the paragraph as `Changelog: none (fixes a fault in an unreleased change).` instead of `Changelog (Fixed): ...`, and in the done record set changelog_kind to "Fixed" and begin `changelog` with "(No entry: a fault in an unreleased change.)" followed by one sentence on what was wrong. The full findings, with the second reviewer's evidence line by line, are in /home/user/polish-tools/review/*.md and *.json (search for the finding ids in brackets). The review read the branch at 7e8df53; other changes have landed since, so read the functions as they are now. Wording only, plus the test expectations that quote it. For 'sorted-cut-ignores-folders-on-top' take the smallest alternative: one sentence in the manual's sort paragraph saying that a sort chooses the items before folders are put on top; do not change the engine. For 'f5-rows-and-mac-only-test' reword the two manual rows only; leave the test. One more sentence from the same review (finding changelog-entries-contradict-each-other, part 4): docs/manual.md says going elsewhere by a click in the sidebar keeps the search in the history, but a click on a Smart Folder that searches This Computer takes the search's place; say 'a folder or place clicked in the sidebar or the path bar' and add 'Opening a Smart Folder that searches This Computer takes the search's place, as typing other words does.' Do not edit CHANGELOG.md. Look at the Search Syntax dialog and the Save Smart Folder dialog in a picture after the change: the longer first row must still fit its column.
